evidence.text: Duplicate invoice-side-effect alerts rose from a baseline of 0-2 per hour to 41 in the first hour after worker release 4.18 reached 60% of workers.
The message broker recorded 37 lease expirations and redeliveries during the same hour; normal is fewer than 3.
For messages that reached the ledger write, the database unique constraint rejected duplicate ledger-row keys; the customer-notification side effect is outside that transaction.
Gateway request logs were retained for only about 30% of tenants because of an unrelated sampling configuration.
For six duplicate notifications, traces show the first worker call waiting on the tax service beyond the 60-second broker lease before a second delivery began.
One fully traced duplicate used the same broker message ID on both worker executions, 63 seconds apart.
For eight affected tenants whose gateway logs were complete, no second client submission occurred in the 10 minutes surrounding the duplicate notification.
The idempotency-cache metrics exporter failed 20 minutes before the incident; hit/miss counters are unavailable for the incident window.
Two sampled workers had NTP offsets below 20 ms. Four other affected workers had no clock telemetry retained.

A staging replay with a deliberately slow tax-service response reproduced lease expiry and redelivery. It did not reproduce a duplicate customer notification while the idempotency cache was known healthy.
Incident-window idempotency-cache request logs had already rotated, so cache availability and key-presence for the affected messages cannot be reconstructed.
Three duplicate notifications were produced by workers that had not yet received release 4.18.
The tax service showed no error-rate increase, but its p99 latency increased from 18 seconds to 74 seconds during the incident.

hypotheses.text: Broker redelivery after lease expiry contributed to duplicate worker execution.
A second client submission was required for the duplicate notifications.
An idempotency-cache miss or outage allowed a duplicate notification after redelivery.
Worker clock skew caused the broker lease expirations.

actions.text: Disable idempotency checks until cache telemetry is restored.
Restore cache observability and preserve cache request logs for subsequent incident analysis.
Disable client-side retries globally during the incident.
Add broker-lease renewal or bound the tax-service wait so long downstream calls cannot silently outlive the lease.
Increase the database unique-key retry count so rejected duplicate ledger writes are retried automatically.
